skill.name: gh
skill.description: Patterns for invoking the GitHub CLI (gh) from agents. Covers structured output, pagination, repo targeting, search vs list, gh api fallback.
skill.summary: Use GitHub CLI with structured output, explicit repository targeting, pagination, and authentication guidance for agent workflows.
skill.author: cli

security_audit.summary: All 226 static findings are false positives: Markdown formatting, a GitHub URL template, authentication documentation, and search error guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent in SKILL.md. The skill documents legitimate GitHub operations, including writes and downloads, which still require user authorization and appropriate permissions.

prompting (e.g. `must provide --title and --body when not running interactively`).
You don't need to defensively set `GH_PAGER` or pass `--no-pager` (no such
Human output from `gh` is column-formatted. If you want structured data:
- Add `--json field1,field2,...` for structured output.
- For `gh issue view` and `gh pr view`, use `--json ...,comments` to include comments in structured
- Run a command with `--json` and **no field list** to print the full set of
- Use `--jq '<expr>'` for filtering without piping through a separate `jq`.
- Use `--template '<go-template>'` (alongside `--json`) when you want shaped
text output. Note that `--template`/`-T` collides with a body-template flag
on a few commands (e.g. `gh pr create -T`, `gh issue create -T`); always
check `--help` before assuming which one you're hitting.
- `gh issue list`, `gh pr list`, `gh search ...`: pass `-L N` (`--limit N`).
- `gh issue list` / `gh pr list` do not expose aggregate totals like
`totalCount` via `--json`. If you need a true total, use `gh api graphql`
to query `totalCount`; otherwise, treat `-L` as the cap for the current call.
- For raw API calls use `gh api --paginate <path>`. Combine with
`--jq` and (optionally) `--slurp` to assemble one array.
`gh` infers the repo from the cwd's git remotes.
Pass `--repo OWNER/REPO` (`-R`) to override the resolved CWD repo.
- `gh search issues|prs|code|repos|commits|users` uses GitHub's search
index and accepts the full search syntax (`is:open`, `author:`,
`label:`, `repo:owner/name`, `in:title`, ...). Pass each qualifier as
`gh search issues repo:cli/cli is:open author:monalisa` works, but
`gh search issues "repo:cli/cli is:open"` is treated as a single keyword (parsed as `repo:"cli/cli i
and fails with `Invalid search query`. Quote only multi-word free text
(`gh search issues "broken feature"`). Most qualifiers also have a
dedicated flag (`--repo`, `--author`, `--label`, ...). Prefer search for
- `gh issue list --search "..."` and `gh pr list --search "..."` take the
- Bots author as GitHub Apps, so `--author dependabot` matches nothing. Use
`--app dependabot` (on `pr`/`issue list` and `search prs|issues`; expands
to `author:app/<slug>`) or `--author "dependabot[bot]"`.
- `gh search issues` also takes `--search-type <lexical|semantic|hybrid>`
(github.com/GHEC only, issues only): use `semantic` when the user describes a
problem in natural language rather than exact terms, and `hybrid` to blend
keyword and semantic ranking; `lexical` (default) is exact matching.

## Issue artifacts (`gh issue artifact`)
(type `generic` or `plan`), HTML documents (type `embedded_html`), and links
(type `link`) attached to an issue. Each has a number on its issue, and
are not GitHub Actions artifacts, which `gh run download` handles.
- `gh issue artifact list {<issue-number>|<issue-url>} [--type generic|plan|link|embedded_html] [--l
(alias `ls`) lists artifacts in number order. There is no default limit:
every artifact is listed unless `--limit` is set. `--type generic` and
`--type plan` both list every Markdown document, and each keeps its stored
update time. `--json` fields include `body`, so one call can return every
- `gh issue artifact view {<issue> <artifact-number> | <artifact-url>} [--version N] [--json <fields
artifact's URL. Piped output is `name:`, `number:`, `version:`, `type:`,
`creator:`, `created:`, `updated-by:`, `updated:`, and `url:` lines, in
that order, then `--` and the raw body. `--version N` shows that version
from the edit history. `--version`, `--json`, and `--web` are mutually
exclusive. `--json versions` returns the edit history. `--web` opens a
- `gh issue artifact create {<issue-number>|<issue-url>} [<file>[#<name>] | <url>]... [--body <text>
(alias `new`) creates one artifact per file or URL, in argument
text following `#`:
`gh issue artifact create 142 'docs/signin-plan.md#Sign-in plan'`. A
`.html` or `.htm` file becomes an HTML document. An
`http(s)` URL becomes a link named after its host, and a `.url` Internet
characters, such as parentheses. `gh` drops them from names it takes from
file names (`plan (1).md` becomes `plan 1.md`), but sends a name given with
`#` or `--name` as typed. Instead of file or URL arguments, `--body <text>`
creates one document and `--body-file <path>` creates one artifact from a
file. Neither can be combined with file or URL arguments. `--name` names a
single artifact. It's required with `--body` or `--body-file -`, and can't
be combined with a `#<name>` suffix. Documents are `generic`, and HTML
documents `embedded_html`. `--type` sets the type of every document
instead, whatever the file extension, so `--type embedded_html` makes
`--body` or `--body-file -` an HTML document. A plan currently behaves the
same as a generic document. `--type` is refused if any artifact is a link.
- `gh issue artifact edit {<issue> <artifact-number> | <artifact-url>} [--name <name>] [--body <text
one of `--name`, `--body`, `--body-file`, `--attach`, or `--restore-version`

- `gh issue artifact delete {<issue> <artifact-number>... | <artifact-url>...} [--yes]`

## Reading files and directories (`gh repo read-file` / `read-dir`)
without cloning, and honor `--repo OWNER/REPO` (`-R`) and `--ref <branch|tag|commit>`
- `gh repo read-file <path> [--ref <ref>] [--output <path> [--clobber]] [--allow-escape-sequences] [
refused; pass `--allow-escape-sequences` to read it anyway. `--output <path>` (`-o`) writes to
remote file name; `--clobber` allows overwrite); writing to disk always
includes the raw bytes regardless of escape sequences. `--output` and `--json` are
mutually exclusive. `--json` fields include `name`, `path`, `gitSHA`, `size`,
`type`, `encoding`, and `content` (base64 encoded).
- `gh repo read-dir [<path>] [--ref <ref>] [--json <fields>] [--jq <expr>]`
separated as type, name, octal mode, and byte size. `--json` fields include
`name`, `path`, `type`, `gitType`, `mode`, `modeOctal`, `gitSHA`, `size`, and
`submodule`. A path pointing at a file errors and points you at `read-file`
## Fall back to `gh api` for anything `--json` doesn't expose
- Review-thread comments on a PR: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/comments`
(the `--comments` flag on `gh pr view` shows issue-level comments only).
- Arbitrary GraphQL: `gh api graphql -f query='...' -F var=value`.
- REST shortcuts: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/...` - note the
`{owner}/{repo}` placeholder is filled in for you when run from a repo
- `gh auth status` prints the active host(s), user, and which env var (if

- Do not cache the output of `gh auth token`: an expiring token can stop

- A `refresh_expired` state in `gh auth status --json hosts` means the refresh
token was rejected. Recovery needs an interactive `gh auth login` or
`gh auth refresh`, so ask the user to run it instead of retrying.
- Tokens from `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` are used as is and never refreshed.
- `gh pr checkout <n>` switches branches. Use `gh pr diff <n>` or
`gh pr view <n>` if you only need to read.
- `gh pr checkout <n> --worktree <path>` checks the PR out into a git worktree
at `<path>` instead of switching the current branch.
- `gh issue develop <n> --checkout` creates a linked branch for the issue and
checks it out. Add `--worktree <path>` to check that branch out into a git
worktree at `<path>` instead of switching the current branch;
`--worktree` requires `--checkout`, cannot be blank, and cannot be combined
with `--list`.

content.user_title: Use GitHub CLI Reliably in Agent Workflows
content.value_statement: GitHub automation can fail when agents parse display output, overlook result limits, or target the wrong repository. This skill provides GitHub CLI patterns for structured queries, pagination, repository selection, and authentication handling.
actual_capabilities: Guides structured GitHub CLI output using selected JSON fields, built-in jq filtering, and Go templates.
Explains result limits, API pagination, aggregate counts, and truncated issue relationships.
Documents explicit repository targeting and search syntax for issues, pull requests, code, and repositories.
Provides command guidance for issue relationships, discussions, attachments, and issue artifacts.
Documents repository file and directory reads without cloning, plus REST and GraphQL fallback queries.
Explains authentication status, token refresh behavior, and checkout alternatives using worktrees.
limitations: Requires an installed GitHub CLI, network access, and credentials with suitable permissions for protected operations.
Preview commands and newer flags may be unavailable in the installed GitHub CLI version.
GitHub Enterprise Server does not support the documented attachment uploads or issue artifacts; other features have host and version requirements.
Provides reference instructions, not executable tooling or enforcement of authorization, upload safety, or output completeness.

use_cases.title: Inspect Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Review changes and retrieve review-thread comments using structured queries without switching the current branch.

use_cases.title: Triage Repository Issues
use_cases.description: Find related issues, inspect dependency relationships, and detect incomplete result sets before planning updates.

use_cases.title: Collect Repository Reports
use_cases.description: Gather selected fields across repositories using search, pagination, and API queries for repeatable reporting.

prompt_templates.title: List Open Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: List up to 20 open issues in [OWNER/REPO] using GitHub CLI. Return issue numbers and titles, and state the result limit.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Read a bounded issue list.

prompt_templates.title: Review Without Checkout
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect pull request [NUMBER] in [OWNER/REPO] without changing branches. Summarize the diff and review-thread comments using structured output and API fallback.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Inspect a pull request without changing the workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Issue Relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect parent, sub-issue, and blocking relationships for issue [NUMBER] in [OWNER/REPO]. Compare returned nodes with totalCount and flag truncation. Make no changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Check issue relationships and completeness.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Paginated Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Report open Dependabot pull requests across [REPOSITORIES] using structured GitHub CLI queries. Handle pagination and explain limits. Prefer gh api without exposing tokens.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Combine repository targeting, bot filters, pagination, and authentication handling.

output_examples.input: Explain how to inspect a pull request without changing branches.
output: Use the pull request view for metadata and the diff view for changed lines.
Retrieve review-thread comments through the pull request comments API.
Avoid checkout when the task only requires inspection.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a 30-item issue list proves the repository has 30 open issues.
output: No. List commands usually cap results at 30 by default.
Increase the explicit limit for a larger sample or use API pagination.
Use a GraphQL total count when an exact aggregate is required.

output_examples.input: Explain what to do when authentication reports refresh_expired.
output: Ask the user to run interactive login or authentication refresh.
Avoid repeated retries and do not request token values.

best_practices: Specify the repository explicitly and request only the structured fields needed for the task.
Set result limits, use pagination when needed, and compare relationship node counts with reported totals.
Confirm authorization before uploads, edits, deletions, or overwrites, and prefer gh api to handling raw tokens.
anti_patterns: Parse display tables or treat a capped result list as a complete repository inventory.
Switch branches for read-only inspection or overwrite local files without approval.
Expose authentication tokens or upload local files without checking their contents and destination.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running commands requires an environment with GitHub CLI access.

faq.question: Does this skill install or authenticate GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: No. It provides command guidance. GitHub CLI must already be installed, and protected operations require suitable authentication.

faq.question: How should agents parse GitHub CLI output?
faq.answer: Request explicit JSON fields and use built-in jq filtering or templates. Avoid parsing human-readable tables.

faq.question: Can it retrieve every matching issue or pull request?
faq.answer: It explains limits and pagination. Completeness depends on command behavior, permissions, service limits, and checking returned counts.

faq.question: Does every documented feature work on GitHub Enterprise Server?
faq.answer: No. Attachment uploads and issue artifacts are unsupported there. Other features depend on server versions, host support, and installed CLI capabilities.

faq.question: Does the skill require sharing GitHub tokens?
faq.answer: No. Prefer authenticated gh api calls. Do not expose token values; ask the user to handle interactive login when recovery requires it.
